title: Register increment and decrement chains
statement: Let $m,k,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and a state set $\Lambda$, let $x$ be a bit string, and fix a register $r$, a direction (increment or decrement), and a sequence of states $(\ell_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$. Suppose that for each $i<k$, the instruction at state $\ell_i$ increments $r$ and goes to $\ell_{i+1}$ in the increment case, or decrements $r$ and goes to $\ell_{i+1}$ in the decrement case. If the initial register values $v$ satisfy $v(s)\le B$ for every register $s$, and additionally $v(r)+k\le B$ in the increment case or $k\le v(r)$ in the decrement case, then the program reaches the configuration with state $\ell_k$, unchanged result field, and register values given by replacing $v(r)$ by $v(r)+k$ or by the truncated difference $v(r)-k$, respectively. Throughout this finite run, every configuration satisfies the program's side conditions and every register value is at most $B$.
